As the monsoon approaches and the salt must be harvested before the rains wash it away, threats turn into sabotage. Shot on location with long, patient takes, the film is a quietly powerful drama about labour, dignity and solidarity among women, building to a tense harvest race against both the weather and the men who want them to fail.

title: Iravu Rail 47
synopsis: Train 47, the overnight express from Chennai to Madurai, leaves Egmore station on time with nine hundred passengers aboard. Somewhere between Villupuram and Tiruchirappalli, a retired judge is found dead in his first-class coupe, its door locked from the inside. Inspector Selvam of the railway police, travelling home on leave, takes charge, knowing that whoever did it is still on the train and could step off at any of the next six stations. His only help comes from Nila, a sharp-tongued medical intern in the next compartment, and a nervous ticket examiner who knows more than he is saying. As the train thunders through the night, every passenger near the coupe turns out to have some link to a case the judge decided twenty years earlier. With the clock ticking toward Madurai, Selvam must untangle the motives before the killer disappears into the morning crowds. The film is a tightly wound whodunit with a single setting and a final reveal staged on a moving footboard.

title: Kolam Pottu Kaathiru
synopsis: Every morning for a month, someone has been drawing an elaborate kolam outside the house of Bhuvana, a software tester who has just moved into a narrow Mylapore street with her elderly grandmother. The designs are beautiful, intricate and clearly meant as messages, but nobody admits to making them. Bhuvana's grandmother is delighted, the neighbours are suspicious, and Bhuvana, who swore off romance after a disastrous engagement, is mostly annoyed. Her investigation narrows the suspects to three men on the street: a shy temple flower seller, a loud insurance agent and Karthi, a struggling architect who lives opposite and claims he cannot draw a straight line. As the Margazhi music season fills the neighbourhood with concerts and competitions, a kolam contest offers the perfect chance to unmask the mystery artist. Light, affectionate and full of colourful neighbourhood characters, the film is a gentle romantic comedy about patience, tradition and the small daily gestures that say more than words ever could.

title: Kadal Thaandiya Kaavalan
synopsis: In 1764, the pearl-fishing villages of the Coromandel coast are squeezed between foreign traders, local chieftains and pirates who raid on moonless nights. Seenu is a young pearl diver who can hold his breath longer than anyone on the coast and has no interest in anybody's war, until a raid destroys his village and his sister is carried off on a foreign ship. Determined to bring her back, he joins a crew of smugglers, outcasts and a disgraced palace guard who know the islands and currents of the Gulf of Mannar. The voyage takes him through storms, sea battles and the treacherous politics of a trading port where human beings are sold alongside spices and pearls. Along the way Seenu becomes the reluctant leader the coastal people have been waiting for. Filmed with large-scale sea sequences and underwater photography, the film is a sweeping period adventure mixing swordplay, naval combat and a heartfelt brother-and-sister story.

title: Daftar No. 13
synopsis: Rohit Bhalla, a lazy junior clerk in the Lucknow municipal corporation, is transferred as punishment to Office Number 13, a dusty room on the top floor of a colonial building that nobody has entered in years. Rumour says it is haunted by Pandeyji, a fiercely honest clerk who died at his desk in 1987 while waiting for a pension file to be signed. On his first day, Rohit finds the files neatly stacked, the tea hot and a note in old-fashioned handwriting demanding that pending applications be cleared by evening. When he ignores it, his chair moves, his phone rings with calls from the past and his corrupt boss starts receiving terrifying visits. Teaming up with Shalini, an idealistic trainee who believes the ghost is on their side, Rohit begins clearing decades of backlog, to the horror of officials who profit from delays. The film is a breezy horror comedy that pokes fun at bureaucracy while finding unexpected warmth in a ghost who still believes in public service.

title: Barf Ki Seedhiyan
synopsis: Pinki Rawat grew up in a village in Uttarakhand watching foreign trekkers walk past her family's tea shop toward the high peaks, and she has always wanted to follow them. When her father, a porter, is killed in an avalanche while carrying supplies for a commercial expedition, her mother forbids her from ever going near the mountains. Years later, working as a cook at a mountaineering institute, Pinki secretly trains at night, running up hillsides with sacks of rice on her back. A burned-out former army climber, Captain Negi, notices her stamina and reluctantly agrees to coach her. Together they set their sights on an unclimbed route on a Himalayan peak, competing against a well-funded team from Delhi with sponsors, cameras and oxygen to spare. The climb becomes a test of endurance, trust and whether Pinki is chasing her own dream or her father's ghost. The film pairs striking high-altitude photography with an intimate story of grief and ambition.

title: Khoya Paya Junction
synopsis: For thirty-four years, Shambhu Prasad has run the lost and found counter at Itarsi Junction, one of the busiest railway crossroads in central India. His cramped office is full of umbrellas, suitcases, dentures, love letters and even a harmonium, each carefully recorded in his handwritten registers. With retirement a month away and his own family barely speaking to him, Shambhu decides to return as many lost items as possible to their owners before he leaves. Helped by his granddaughter Guddi, a college student with a talent for social media, he begins tracing owners across the country. Each delivery opens a small story: a soldier's lost medal, a bride's misplaced jewellery box and a cassette recorded by a mother who died years ago. As the pair travel by train from town to town, Shambhu is forced to face the one thing he lost long ago and never tried to find, his bond with his estranged son. The film is a gentle, episodic comedy-drama about memory and reconnection.

title: Raakh Aur Roshni
synopsis: Bombay, 1946. As India stands on the edge of independence, Haroon Siddiqui is an idealistic young printer whose small press turns out pamphlets for union leaders, poets and nationalist students. His closest friend, Vasant Desai, writes fiery editorials that the colonial police want silenced. When a naval mutiny erupts in the city's harbour and unrest spreads through the streets, both men are swept into events far bigger than themselves. Haroon falls for Nargis, a radio announcer whose broadcasts carry coded messages, and the three become involved in hiding a fugitive sailor. As communal tensions rise over the following months and the city divides along lines that would have seemed impossible a year earlier, the friendship between Haroon and Vasant is tested by fear, rumour and loyalty to their own communities. Lavishly recreating old Bombay, the film is an ambitious period drama about friendship, free speech and the price of freedom, told through people history rarely remembers.

title: Godavari Gaali Patam
synopsis: Every Sankranti, the Kothapalli family gathers at their ancestral house on the banks of the Godavari near Rajahmundry, and every year the festival ends in an argument. This time the patriarch, Ramachandra Rao, announces that he wants to sell the house and divide the money, shocking his three children, who have been quietly counting on it for their own reasons. Software engineer Ravi needs funds for a start-up in Bengaluru, his sister Lakshmi wants to stay and turn the house into a homestay, and the youngest, Chinna, has secretly borrowed against it. Into this chaos arrives Sirisha, a sharp young lawyer from Hyderabad sent to prepare the sale documents, who finds herself drawn into family secrets, kite-flying battles and a fiercely competitive rangoli contest. Over four days of feasting, music and squabbling, old wounds are reopened and slowly healed. The film is a colourful festival comedy-drama about inheritance, belonging and what really holds a family together.

title: Nallamala Rahasyam
synopsis: Forest ranger Vikram has spent eight years guarding the Nallamala hills, where tiger reserves, ancient cave temples and illegal mines sit uncomfortably close together. When a team of archaeologists disappears near a newly discovered rock-cut shrine, he is ordered to lead the search, accompanied by Dr Meghana, a sharp epigraphist who believes the shrine's inscriptions point to a buried temple treasury mentioned in medieval records. They are not the only ones looking. A mining contractor with political backing has sent armed men into the forest, and the local forest communities, whose land the hills are, want outsiders to keep away from their sacred sites. As monsoon storms close the roads and the radio goes silent, the search becomes a deadly race through caves, waterfalls and tiger country. Vikram must decide whether he is protecting the forest, the treasure or the people who belong there. The film is a rousing jungle adventure that blends mythology, action and a strong ecological message.

title: Mallepoola Manasu
synopsis: Seenu sells jasmine garlands outside a temple in Vijayawada and sings while he strings the flowers, with a voice that stops passers-by in their tracks. Every morning a classical violinist named Gayatri, who teaches at a music academy across the road, buys a single string of jasmine from him and never says a word. When Gayatri hears him sing at a local festival, she offers to train him for a prestigious music competition in Hyderabad, provided he sets aside the film songs he loves and learns the discipline of Carnatic music. Their lessons, held at dawn on the riverbank, slowly turn into something deeper, but class differences, family expectations and Seenu's pride stand in the way. Gayatri, meanwhile, is hiding a medical condition that threatens her own career as a performer. Built around a rich original soundtrack that blends classical ragas with popular melodies, the film is a tender musical romance about talent, devotion and the courage to be heard.

title: Bisi Bele Bath Brothers
synopsis: Two estranged brothers inherit their late father's tiny, beloved breakfast restaurant in Basavanagudi, famous for a single dish that people queue for every morning. Elder brother Prakash, an accountant in Pune, wants to sell it to a coffee chain, while younger brother Sunil, an unemployed food vlogger, wants to keep it and make it famous online. Neither of them can cook. Their father's recipe was never written down, and the only person who knows it, the restaurant's ageing head cook Ramanna, has left on an indefinite pilgrimage after a quarrel. As the brothers try to keep the shutters open, they burn rice, offend regulars, battle food inspectors and become an accidental internet sensation for all the wrong reasons. A cheerful young caterer, Anusha, agrees to help them, but only if they stop fighting. The film is a warm, comic tale about brothers, food and the flavours that tie a neighbourhood together, with a climax set during a busy temple festival morning.

title: Kempu Kallina Kote
synopsis: When a heritage conservation team begins restoring a crumbling red-stone fort near Chitradurga, a worker falls from the ramparts and dies, and the villagers say the fort's guardian spirit has woken. Deputy Superintendent Akshay Rao is sent to close the case quickly before it frightens away investors planning a luxury resort nearby. Working with Bhoomika, a young conservation architect who knows every hidden passage of the fort, he discovers that the death was no accident and that an old map hidden in the walls has attracted dangerous interest. As more strange incidents follow, Akshay has to separate local legends about a palace treasure from very modern motives involving land deals, forged documents and a powerful family with deep roots in the region. Atmospheric and well paced, the film moves between the present-day investigation and a parallel story set during an eighteenth-century siege, gradually revealing how the two are connected through the fort's long and bloody history.

title: Hakki Goodina Haadu
synopsis: Seventy-eight-year-old Narasimhaiah and his wife Saroja live alone in a large old house in Shivamogga, their three children scattered across Bengaluru, Dubai and New Jersey. Their days follow a gentle routine of temple visits, crossword puzzles and long phone calls that the children keep cutting short. When Saroja is diagnosed with early memory loss, Narasimhaiah decides not to tell the children and to care for her himself, leaving handwritten notes around the house to help her remember. A young neighbour, Kaveri, a nursing student who rents the upstairs room, notices what is happening and quietly begins to help. As Saroja's memory fades and returns, she asks to revisit the places where their life together began, and the old man sets off with her on a series of small journeys across the Malnad region. When the children finally learn the truth, they must decide what they owe their parents. Tender and unhurried, the film is a moving portrait of love in old age.

title: Saltwater Ledger
synopsis: In a fading fishing town on the coast of Maine, Jack Merrow keeps the books for the last cannery still operating, a quiet job he took after leaving the navy. One winter night he notices that the cannery's figures do not add up: tons of fish are being bought from boats that never left the harbour. Before he can ask questions, the cannery's owner is found dead in the icy water beneath the pier, and the local police are quick to call it an accident. Jack's sister Nora, a former reporter who has come home to care for their sick mother, suspects otherwise. As the siblings dig into the ledgers, they uncover a smuggling operation that reaches far beyond the town and discover that half their neighbours are either involved or afraid. With a storm closing the roads and the harbour, Jack has to decide whom he can trust. Moody and slow-burning, the film is a small-town crime thriller about debt, loyalty and the secrets communities keep to survive.

title: The Orchard at Kestrel Hill
synopsis: When their grandfather dies, three adult siblings who have not been in the same room for a decade return to the family apple orchard in the hills of Herefordshire to settle his estate. Emma, the eldest, is a hospital administrator in London who wants to sell quickly. Tom, the middle child, never left the village and has been running the orchard on almost no money. Lily, the youngest, is a musician just back from a long tour, carrying a secret she has told no one. Their grandfather's will contains an unusual condition: the orchard cannot be sold until the siblings have brought in one final harvest together. Through a long, golden autumn of picking, pressing cider and arguing about the past, old resentments surface alongside forgotten memories of the summers they spent there as children. A local cider maker and a nosy solicitor add comic friction. Gentle and beautifully photographed, the film is a heartfelt family drama about grief, inheritance and the seasons of a shared life.

title: Last Light at Halcyon Station
synopsis: Halcyon Station is a research outpost orbiting Saturn's moon Titan, home to a crew of six who have spent three years studying the moon's methane seas. Two weeks before they are due to be relieved, a solar storm cripples the station's communications and damages the shuttle meant to take them home. Commander Elias Kane decides to ration power and wait for rescue, but the station's systems begin behaving strangely, opening airlocks, rerouting oxygen and erasing logs. Some of the crew suspect a software fault, while the biologist, Dr Amara Osei, believes something in the samples they brought up from the surface is responsible. As supplies dwindle and trust breaks down, the crew must work out whether the threat is mechanical, biological or one of them. Claustrophobic and tense, the film is a science-fiction survival thriller that balances its mysteries with characters who are exhausted, frightened and desperate to see Earth again, building to a daring attempt to reach the damaged shuttle.

title: Thattukada Republic
synopsis: Every evening at seven, Basheer opens his thattukada, a roadside food cart, on a busy corner of Kozhikode beach road, and by eight the queue for his beef fry and porottas stretches past the bus stop. When the city corporation announces a beautification drive that would clear all street vendors from the beach, Basheer's cart becomes the last one standing after he chains it to a lamppost and refuses to move. What begins as one man's stubbornness turns into a citywide spectacle. Television channels set up cameras, students start a hashtag, three political parties try to claim him as their own, and a young municipal officer, Anjali, is told to end the standoff without turning him into a martyr. As the days pass, the cart becomes an open-air parliament where fishermen, auto drivers, tourists and food bloggers argue about everything from public space to the price of onions. Sharp, affectionate and very funny, the film is a satire about politics, media and the right to make a living.

title: Kaavu Theendal
synopsis: A Kochi real-estate company buys an old ancestral property in rural Palakkad and plans to turn it into a gated villa community. The only obstacle is a small sacred grove at the edge of the land, a tangle of ancient trees, serpent stones and oil lamps that the local family lit every evening for generations. Project engineer Arun dismisses the warnings of the elderly caretaker and orders the grove cleared. Within days, workers fall ill, machines fail at the same spot and cobras appear inside locked site offices. Arun's wife Reshma, an anthropologist who joins him for the holidays, begins recording the stories of women in the village and uncovers a darker history about the family that once owned the land and a girl who vanished there decades earlier. As the monsoon arrives, the line between folklore and guilt becomes harder to see. Moody and atmospheric, the film is a slow-burn horror thriller about greed, ecology and the debts that old places never forget.

title: Pathinaalam Raavu
synopsis: Kochi, 1974. On the fourteenth night of a dock workers' strike, a ship's agent is found stabbed in a godown on Willingdon Island, and the police are eager to pin the murder on the union leader who has been leading the protests. Sub-inspector Mathew Kuruvila, newly transferred from Kottayam and known for refusing bribes, is not convinced. His investigation takes him through the crowded lanes of Mattancherry, smoky toddy shops, Anglo-Indian dance halls and the offices of shipping magnates who want the strike broken at any cost. He finds an unlikely ally in Lucy, a sharp-witted typist at a shipping company who has noticed irregularities in the cargo manifests. As he gets closer to the truth, Mathew realises that the murder is tied to a smuggling ring protected by people far above his rank. Shot in warm period colours with a jazzy score, the film is a stylish retro crime drama about integrity, class and a port city on the brink of change.

title: Kunjikkiliyude Kappal
synopsis: Eleven-year-old Kunjikkili lives with her grandmother on a narrow strip of land between the backwaters near Alappuzha, where every child dreams of rowing in the great snake boat races. Girls are not allowed in the village boat, so Kunjikkili decides to build her own. With the help of her best friend Appu, an old carpenter who once built racing boats and a pile of borrowed planks, she sets out to finish a small boat before the children's race at the Onam festival. The project brings trouble from every side: mocking cousins, a disapproving headmaster, a leaking hull and a flood that nearly washes everything away. Slowly, though, the village begins to rally behind the stubborn girl, and her grandmother reveals a secret from her own childhood on the river. Bright, funny and full of water and song, the film is a heartwarming children's adventure about courage, community and refusing to accept that some things are simply not meant for you.

title: Ezhaam Saakshi
synopsis: Advocate Revathy Menon has never won a big case. When a young domestic worker from Jharkhand is accused of murdering her elderly employer in a wealthy Thiruvananthapuram bungalow, no senior lawyer wants the brief, and the court assigns it to her. The prosecution has six witnesses who place the accused at the scene, a confession signed in police custody and fierce public anger stoked by television debates. Revathy, still living down her own father's disgrace as a lawyer, starts digging into details nobody else bothered with: the victim's tangled property dispute, a missing CCTV recording, and a seventh witness whose name appears in the first police report and then vanishes from every later document. Her search for that witness puts her career, her family and her safety at risk. Built around tense courtroom exchanges and patient investigation, the film is a gripping legal drama about prejudice, migrant labour and whether justice can survive the pressure of public opinion.

title: Kaalai Ezhu Mani
synopsis: Saravanan delivers food on a scooter across Chennai for eleven hours a day to pay off his late father's debts. At seven one morning, while dropping off a breakfast order at a high-rise in Nungambakkam, he sees a man pushed from a fourteenth-floor balcony. The police arrive quickly and declare it a suicide, and Saravanan's statement is waved away. That evening someone breaks into his room, and the delivery app suddenly suspends his account. Convinced he witnessed a murder and now a target himself, he teams up with Divya, a customer care executive at the delivery company who can see the order logs that place him at the scene. Together they reconstruct the dead man's last day using GPS records, restaurant receipts and the routes of other riders. The chase sends them through flyovers, fish markets and gated apartment complexes. Lean and fast-moving, the film is a contemporary thriller about the invisible workers who keep a city fed and the things they see.

title: Saadugudu Seemai
synopsis: In a dusty village near Madurai, schoolteacher Meenakshi coaches girls in kabaddi after classes, on a ground the panchayat keeps trying to turn into a parking lot. Her team is good, but nobody in the village takes them seriously, least of all the fathers who want their daughters married before they turn eighteen. When a state-level tournament offers prize money and scholarships, Meenakshi sees a way to keep her best players in school. The team includes Selvi, a fierce raider whose father has already fixed her wedding date, and Pandi, a quiet defender who works at a brick kiln before dawn. Training under Thambi, a former national player who drinks too much and resents being asked for help, the girls face injuries, family pressure and a rival team backed by a wealthy sports club. Earthy, energetic and full of breathless matches, the film is a rousing sports drama about girls claiming their place on the field and in their own futures.

title: Robo Paati
synopsis: When Chennai software engineer Anand moves to Singapore for work, he worries about his seventy-five-year-old grandmother living alone in their old house in Triplicane. His solution is an experimental home-assistance robot built by a start-up whose founder owes him a favour. The robot is supposed to remind her about medicines and call for help in emergencies. Instead, Paati teaches it to make filter coffee, drags it to temple festivals, enrols it in a neighbourhood quiz team and starts using it to settle scores with the bickering neighbours. The robot, learning from her every day, begins developing opinions of its own, especially about Anand's habit of never calling home. Trouble arrives when the start-up's investors want the robot back to study its unexpected behaviour, and Paati flatly refuses to give up her new companion. Bright, warm-hearted and full of gentle jokes, the film is a family comedy about loneliness, technology and the kinds of care that cannot be programmed.

title: Royapuram Rajyam
synopsis: In the 1990s, two friends grow up around the fishing harbour of Royapuram in north Chennai: Sekar, who wants to become a footballer, and Kumar, who wants to become rich. When a local don recruits Kumar to run diesel smuggling from the harbour, Sekar follows him out of loyalty, and over twenty years the pair build an empire of boats, ration-card scams and property deals that reaches deep into politics. Sekar's wife Ponni, a schoolteacher, has watched the violence seep into her classroom and wants her husband out before their son is drawn in. When a new police commissioner launches a crackdown and offers immunity to anyone willing to talk, the two friends must decide whether their bond is stronger than their fear. Told in chapters that span three decades, the film is a gritty, dialogue-driven gangster saga about friendship, ambition and the neighbourhood that shaped both men, with the harbour itself a vivid presence in almost every scene.

title: Chhoti Si Sarkar
synopsis: When the elected head of a small village in Madhya Pradesh is suspended for corruption, the district collector, a reformer with a flair for publicity, launches an unusual experiment: for one month, the school's children's parliament will run the panchayat under adult supervision. Thirteen-year-old Pooja is elected sarpanch, with her rival Golu as deputy, and the children quickly start doing things the adults never managed, from fixing the hand pump to painting the village budget on the school wall. Their energy embarrasses the suspended sarpanch's family, who begin plotting to sabotage the experiment, while a television crew turns the children into minor celebrities. As the month goes on, Pooja discovers that governing is much harder than giving speeches, especially when her own father turns out to be part of the problem. Light, sunny and pointed, the film is a family satire about democracy, honesty and the possibility that children understand fairness better than grown-ups do.

title: Dhundh Ke Us Paar
synopsis: After a breakdown ends her career as a crime reporter in Delhi, Kavya Sharma takes a winter job as caretaker of a shuttered colonial hotel above Shimla, hoping the silence will help her sleep. The only other people on the property are an elderly gardener and his deaf grandson. On her third night, through the fog, she sees a woman in a red shawl walking along the cliff path and vanishing at the edge. The gardener insists that nobody has stayed at the hotel for years. As the fog thickens and the phone lines fail, Kavya finds a guest register containing entries in her own handwriting, dated twenty years ago. Her digging into the hotel's past leads to a society wedding that ended in a disappearance and to a local police officer who closed the case far too quickly. Unsure whether she is uncovering a crime or losing her grip on reality, she must find out who the woman in the fog really is. The film is an eerie, slow-tightening psychological thriller.

title: Lal Batti Hari Batti
synopsis: Head constable Bhanwar Singh has directed traffic at the same chaotic Delhi intersection for twenty-two years and knows every driver who has ever jumped his signal. Ajju is a cab driver with a loud horn, a louder mouth and a habit of talking his way out of fines. When a routine argument at the signal ends with both men accidentally witnessing a hit-and-run involving a minister's nephew, they become the only two people who can identify the car. Neither trusts the other, but with threats coming from all sides, they end up on a frantic, comic journey across the city in Ajju's battered cab, trying to stay alive long enough to testify. Along the way they visit Bhanwar's estranged daughter, dodge crooked policemen, survive a wedding procession and learn uncomfortable truths about each other. Warm, chaotic and full of Delhi's colour, the film is an odd-couple comedy about honesty, rules and the people who keep a city moving.

title: Andaman Ki Chitthiyan
synopsis: In 1932, Ramnath Mishra, a young schoolteacher from Kanpur accused of printing revolutionary pamphlets, is sentenced to transportation for life and shipped to the Cellular Jail in Port Blair. Before he leaves, he promises his new wife Shanti that he will write to her every week. Prisoners are allowed only the rarest of letters, so Ramnath begins smuggling his out with the help of a sympathetic cook and, later, a guard with his own reasons for helping. In Kanpur, Shanti reads the letters aloud to the women of her neighbourhood, and they slowly become a source of courage for people far beyond her home. The film moves between the harsh routines of the jail, with its oil mills and solitary cells, and Shanti's growing independence in a city stirred by the freedom movement. Decades later, a granddaughter discovers the bundle of letters. The film is a moving period romance about separation, endurance and words that refuse to be silenced.

title: Mirchi Yard
synopsis: Guntur's chilli market is one of the largest in Asia, and for thirty years its trade has been controlled by Venkatadri, a commission agent who decides who buys, who sells and at what price. When a cyclone ruins the crop and farmers are pushed deep into debt, Krishna, a loader in the market yard with a temper as fiery as the produce he carries, starts organising the farmers to sell directly to exporters. His rebellion threatens Venkatadri's empire, and the old man's sons respond with intimidation and violence. Krishna's childhood friend Padma, now a reporter with a local news channel, begins investigating the cartel's links to politicians and banks. As the conflict escalates, the market yard becomes a battleground, with clashes among mountains of red chillies, warehouse fires and a hostage crisis during the peak trading season. Loud, colourful and built around a crowd-pleasing hero, the film is a mass action drama about farmers, middlemen and who really profits from the land.

title: Vennela Veedhi
synopsis: Kiran, a struggling stand-up comedian in Hyderabad, moves into a cheap rented room on a narrow street in the old city where the power goes out every night at ten. His neighbour across the balcony is Swapna, a night-shift nurse who comes home at dawn and is furious about the noise he makes rehearsing jokes. Their constant bickering slowly turns into a nightly ritual: when the lights go out, the two talk across the gap between their balconies in the moonlight, sharing stories about their families, their failures and the lives they wanted. Kiran begins using their conversations in his act, which suddenly becomes funnier and more honest, but he does not tell Swapna that she has become his material. When a video of his routine goes viral and she recognises herself in it, their friendship is put to the test. Charming and unhurried, the film is a sweet romantic comedy about two lonely people, filled with the sights and sounds of Hyderabad after dark.

title: Rendo Suryudu
synopsis: Dr Aditya Rao is a solar physicist at the space centre in Sriharikota, working on a small satellite designed to study storms on the sun. When the instrument picks up an unusual pattern in the solar wind, he becomes convinced that a massive solar storm is coming, one that could knock out power grids and communications across half the planet. His seniors dismiss his data, foreign agencies stay silent, and his obsession is straining his marriage to Usha, a schoolteacher in Nellore who is raising their son almost alone. Aditya teams up with a young engineer, Pallavi, and an old mentor who was forced into early retirement, to prove his theory and find a way to protect the country's grid in the few weeks left. The film follows their race against bureaucracy and time, balancing scientific detail with the quieter story of a family learning to understand a man who keeps staring at the sky. It is a thoughtful, hopeful science drama about curiosity and responsibility.

title: Peddamma Pickles
synopsis: Sixty-eight-year-old Annapurna, called Peddamma by everyone in her town near Ongole, has been making mango, gongura and lemon pickles for weddings and neighbours for forty years. When her son loses his job in Bengaluru and the family house is threatened by a loan, her granddaughter Hasini, a business student, suggests turning the pickles into a proper company. With a borrowed van, a hand-painted label and an online store that keeps crashing, the family stumbles into the world of start-ups, food licences and courier companies. Peddamma refuses to change her recipes, argues with investors and becomes a minor celebrity after one of her cooking videos goes viral. A big packaged-food company soon offers to buy the brand, but only if the recipes can be standardised in a factory. The film follows the family's struggle to grow without losing what made them special, mixing kitchen-table comedy with gentle drama about ageing, pride and the value of things made by hand.

title: Kambala Kesari
synopsis: In a village near Udupi, the Kambala buffalo races held across slushy paddy fields every winter are more than a sport: they are a matter of family honour. Sathish, a young jockey from a poor family, has the speed and nerve to win but no buffaloes of his own, and he races for an arrogant landlord who takes all the credit. When the landlord humiliates him after a narrow loss, Sathish quits and decides to train a pair of untested young buffaloes bought with his mother's savings. Helped by Rekha, a veterinary student who knows more about animals than racing, and an old trainer who once won the most famous race on the coast, he prepares for the season's biggest event. Along the way he faces debt, sabotage and a court case challenging the sport itself. Splashing through mud, music and coastal festivals, the film is an exhilarating sports drama that captures the pride and rivalries of the Tulu Nadu countryside.

title: Silk Board Signal
synopsis: At six on a rainy Friday evening, the Silk Board junction in Bengaluru is jammed solid, and nobody is going anywhere for at least two hours. Trapped in neighbouring vehicles are a start-up founder on the way to pitch to investors, a nervous groom heading to his own engagement, a cab driver with a mysterious bag in his boot, a retired couple arguing about a missed flight and a young woman who has just quit her job and is livestreaming the jam. When the cab driver's bag starts ringing and a police officer begins checking vehicles one by one, the strangers are pulled into a farcical crime caper that unfolds entirely within the gridlock. Alliances form and break across car windows, delivery riders squeeze between bumpers, and a stray cow plays a crucial role. Told in real time and bursting with local humour, the film is a madcap ensemble comedy about the city's traffic, its ambitions and the unlikely connections made while standing completely still.

title: Yakshagana Raatri
synopsis: For three generations, a small Yakshagana troupe has travelled through coastal Karnataka performing all-night dance dramas drawn from the epics. Now the troupe's master, Gopala Bhat, is ill, the audiences are shrinking and the young performers are leaving for jobs in Bengaluru and the Gulf. His granddaughter Anjali, a software engineer who was never encouraged to perform, returns home to help shut the troupe down. Instead, she finds herself drawn into the rehearsals, the elaborate make-up rituals and the thundering music of the chende drums. When the troupe receives an invitation to perform at a prestigious festival, Anjali decides to revive it, recruiting old members, training new ones and challenging customs that some in the village are unwilling to see changed. Rich with colour, costume and performance, the film is a heartfelt drama about art, inheritance and the courage to reinterpret a tradition without losing its soul, culminating in a spectacular performance that lasts until dawn.

title: Neeli Mane
synopsis: Sowmya, a young widow, moves into a blue-painted bungalow on the outskirts of Sakleshpur with her eight-year-old son, renting it cheaply from an estate owner who is oddly eager to have tenants. The house sits among misty coffee plantations, and at first it seems the perfect place to start over. Soon her son starts talking to a girl nobody else can see, the doors open by themselves at three in the morning, and the blue walls begin to peel to reveal handwriting underneath. The plantation workers refuse to come near the house after dark. Sowmya's search for answers leads her to an old estate clerk and a family scandal from the 1970s involving a missing governess. As the hauntings grow more violent, she must decide whether to flee or to finish what the house seems to be asking of her. Built on creaking floorboards, rain and silence rather than cheap shocks, the film is an old-fashioned haunted-house horror with a strong emotional core.

title: Ink and Longitude
synopsis: In 1768, Eleanor Ashby, the daughter of a disgraced London mapmaker, disguises herself as a young man to join a naval expedition charting the islands of the South Pacific. Her father was ruined when a map he drew led a ship onto a reef, and she is determined to prove that the fault lay with someone else. On board she becomes assistant to the expedition's astronomer, a gruff Frenchman testing a new clock that might finally solve the problem of measuring longitude at sea. As the voyage passes through storms, mutiny and encounters with island communities whose navigators know the ocean far better than the Europeans do, Eleanor discovers that her father's ruin was linked to a powerful patron now funding this very expedition. Keeping her identity hidden becomes harder with every week at sea. Handsomely mounted and rich in seafaring detail, the film is a historical adventure about science, ambition and the quiet bravery of a woman doing work the world would not allow her to do.

title: Four Floors Down
synopsis: Every night at two, the vault beneath the Garrick Building in downtown Chicago is opened for exactly nine minutes while the night shift transfers cash for the city's armoured trucks. Mara Quill, a former structural engineer turned thief, has spent a year planning a heist that does not involve the vault door at all: her crew will come up through the floor from an abandoned freight tunnel four storeys below the street. The team includes a nervous tunnel worker, an ex-cop with gambling debts, a teenage hacker and Mara's estranged brother, the only person she trusts and the one she least wants to involve. On the night of the job, a flash flood starts filling the tunnels, a hostage situation erupts upstairs, and it becomes clear that someone on the inside has sold them out. Tense and tightly plotted, the film is a ticking-clock heist thriller that unfolds almost entirely underground, where every wrong move could bring the city down on top of them.

title: Pebble and the Lantern Fox
synopsis: Pebble is a small, curious hedgehog who lives in a valley where the animals are afraid of the dark and hurry home before sunset. When the valley's ancient beacon, a giant glowing mushroom on the hilltop, begins to fade, the elders announce that the long night is coming and that nothing can be done. Pebble refuses to believe them. She sets out with Wick, a nervous young fox whose tail glows faintly in the dark, to find the source of the light in the far mountains. Their journey takes them across a river of fireflies, through a library run by owls and into the caves of a grumpy badger who claims to be a scientist. Along the way, Pebble learns that her new friend's glow is fading too, and that courage sometimes means admitting you are frightened. Bright, gentle and beautifully animated, the film is a family adventure about friendship, fear of the dark and the small lights people carry for one another.

title: Love All, Lose Nothing
synopsis: At thirty-three, Priya Raman is about to retire from professional tennis after years of injuries and early exits, ranked too low to enter the big tournaments without a wildcard. Her final event is a small grass-court tournament on the English coast, where she expects to lose in the first round and quietly go home. Instead, she keeps winning. Paired in the mixed doubles with Leo Marchetti, a charming but undisciplined young player just back from a suspension for a temper tantrum, she rediscovers a joy in the game she thought she had lost. As the tournament progresses, her former coach and ex-husband turns up in the box of her next opponent, and a sports journalist begins writing about her unlikely run. Priya has to decide whether this is a fairy-tale ending or a reason to keep going. Light on its feet and generous with its characters, the film is a sports romance about second chances, pride and loving something enough to let it go.

title: Kallu Shappile Kavitha
synopsis: Unnikrishnan once won a state award for poetry as a college student, but twenty years later he pours toddy at a roadside shop on a canal bank in Kuttanad, reciting verses to customers who mostly want more fish curry. When a young literary researcher, Aswathy, arrives from Thiruvananthapuram to write a thesis on forgotten poets of the 1990s, she is astonished to find her subject working behind the counter. She persuades him to perform at a literature festival in Kozhikode, but the shop's owner, its regulars and Unnikrishnan's own fear of failing again all stand in the way. Meanwhile the shop itself faces closure under new licensing rules, and its motley customers, a retired postman, a boat driver and a lovesick tailor, decide to fight for it. Wry, warm and full of music and verse, the film is a gentle comedy-drama about lost ambition, the dignity of ordinary work and the poetry hidden in everyday conversation.

title: Munnar Mist Murders
synopsis: A wealthy tea planter invites his estranged children, his business partner and his new young wife to his bungalow above Munnar to celebrate his seventieth birthday. By morning he is dead at the bottom of a ravine, and a landslide has cut the only road down the mountain. Circle inspector Jacob Varghese, staying at a nearby homestay on a fishing holiday, is the only officer who can reach the estate. With the help of the family's sharp-eyed young cook, Ammini, he interviews the guests one by one in the fog-bound house. Each has a motive: a disputed will, a secret sale of estate land, an accident covered up years earlier. When a second guest disappears in the mist, Jacob realises that the killer is still among them and that the road will not reopen for two more days. A classic country-house whodunit transplanted to the Western Ghats, the film delights in red herrings, rain-soaked atmosphere and a final gathering of suspects.

title: Abudhabiyil Ninnoru Kathu
synopsis: Sasidharan has worked as a mechanic in Abu Dhabi for twenty-two years, sending money home to Kannur, building his family a house he has lived in for a total of eleven months, and paying for his sister's wedding and his children's education. Now, at fifty-four, he has been laid off and is coming home for good. His wife Shobha, who has run the household alone for two decades, is not sure how to make room for him. His teenage son treats him like a guest, and his daughter is planning a life in Canada. The village, which once greeted him as a rich returnee, quickly loses interest once it learns there is no more money. Sasidharan tries to find a place for himself, opening a small workshop, joining a returnees' association and reconnecting with an old friend who never left. Built around a letter he wrote but never posted, the film is a quietly moving family drama about migration and what it costs both those who leave and those who wait.

title: Chuvanna Mudi
synopsis: For eleven months of the year, Kannan works as a daily-wage labourer on construction sites in Kannur, treated as invisible by the contractors and homeowners he builds for. For a few nights during the Theyyam season, he becomes a god. Painted, crowned and possessed in the eyes of the devotees, he is worshipped by the same upper-caste families who would never let him into their kitchens. When a wealthy family asks him to perform at their newly renovated shrine, Kannan's son Akhil, a college student influenced by activist friends, argues that the arrangement is humiliating and that his father should refuse. Kannan, torn between a sacred duty inherited from his ancestors and his son's anger, prepares for the performance as tensions rise in the village. Shot amid flaming torches, drums and elaborate costumes, the film is a powerful drama about faith, caste, art and dignity, and about a father and son trying to understand each other's idea of respect.

title: Super Sharafu
synopsis: Sharafudheen, known to everyone as Sharafu, is an unremarkable electrician in a small Malappuram town whose biggest ambition is to open a mobile phone repair shop. One night during a thunderstorm, he is struck by lightning while fixing a transformer and wakes up in hospital with a strange ability: he can control electricity with his hands. At first he uses it for small things, charging phones, fixing streetlights and impressing Rasiya, the teacher he has loved since school. But when a ruthless sand-mining contractor begins terrorising the riverside villages, people start whispering about a masked figure who shorts out lorries and blacks out illegal camps. Sharafu's double life gets complicated as his overprotective mother, a nosy local reporter and the contractor's hired goons all close in on his secret. Packed with homegrown action, small-town humour and a big-hearted hero, the film is a family superhero comedy about ordinary people who become extraordinary when their community needs them.

title: Thangamani Talkies
synopsis: Thangamani Talkies has stood at the centre of a small town near Kumbakonam since 1968, showing everything from mythologicals to action blockbusters on a single giant screen. Its ageing owner, Paramasivam, still climbs to the projection room every evening, even though most shows now draw fewer than twenty people. When his son in Chennai arranges to sell the building to a supermarket chain, Paramasivam has three months until the final show. His granddaughter Kayal, an aspiring filmmaker visiting for the summer, decides to give the theatre a proper farewell. With the help of the elderly projectionist, a ticket-seller who has worked there for forty years and a group of local film fans, she organises a festival of the town's favourite films. As the townspeople come back to share memories of first dates, family outings and fights in the queue, the old cinema begins to come alive again. The film is a tender, funny love letter to single-screen theatres and the communities they created.

title: Nizhal Vettai
synopsis: A string of suicides among young IT employees in Chennai looks unconnected until cyber-crime inspector Raghav notices that every victim had been talking to the same anonymous account on a gaming platform. The account seems to know everything about its targets, from their debts to their private photos, and it pushes them through a series of escalating challenges. Raghav's unit is understaffed, and his superiors want the case closed quietly before it embarrasses a major tech company. He is helped by Malar, a former ethical hacker now working in the police lab, who has her own reasons for wanting to find the person behind the account. Their investigation moves from server rooms to gaming cafés and into a murky web of loan apps and data brokers. As they get closer, the hunter begins targeting Raghav's own family. Fast-paced and unsettling, the film is a cyber thriller about surveillance, loneliness and the hidden cost of living our lives online.

title: Kaveri Thottam
synopsis: When the river fails to reach the tail-end villages of the Kaveri delta for a third straight year, farmer Rajendran watches his paddy fields crack and his neighbours sell their land to brick kilns and property agents. His daughter Ezhil, an agricultural science graduate, returns from Coimbatore with ideas about water-saving methods and new crops, which her father dismisses as textbook talk. As debts pile up and a local politician offers to buy the whole village's land for an industrial project, father and daughter are forced to work together. Ezhil revives an old network of village ponds and channels that her grandfather once maintained, organising reluctant farmers and facing resistance from the politician's men. The film moves through the farming calendar, from the first ploughing to an anxious harvest, capturing the rhythms of delta life and the politics of water. It is a sincere, hopeful family drama about land, knowledge passed between generations and a community's struggle to survive drought.

title: Mokka Podcast
synopsis: Four unemployed friends in Coimbatore, tired of being lectured by relatives about their careers, decide to start a podcast. They have no equipment, no guests and no idea what to talk about, so they record in a borrowed wedding hall using a mobile phone and discuss whatever comes to mind: bad first dates, strict fathers, the best parotta in town. Their first episodes are heard by exactly eleven people. Then a rant about a local politician's potholed road goes viral, and suddenly they have sponsors, angry phone calls and an invitation to interview a film star. The sudden fame strains their friendship, especially when one of them is offered a solo deal by a big digital company. Meanwhile, the politician they mocked decides to sue. Packed with quick-fire jokes, local slang and affectionate ribbing of internet culture, the film is a lively buddy comedy about friendship, ambition and working out what you actually have to say.

title: Parchhaiyon Ka Shehar
synopsis: Bombay, 1962. Private detective Vikram Rao spends his days chasing unfaithful husbands and his nights drinking in Irani cafés. When a nervous singer from a Grant Road nightclub hires him to find her missing sister, he expects a routine case. Instead, he finds the sister dead in a rented room in Colaba and a trail that leads to a film producer, a smuggler of gold watches and a respected industrialist with friends in government. As the city braces for war on the northern border and the newspapers fill with patriotic headlines, Vikram uncovers a blackmail racket built on photographs taken in the city's most exclusive hotels. Every lead he follows seems to end in another body, and the singer who hired him is not telling him everything. Shot in moody monochrome tones with a jazz-and-qawwali score, the film is a stylish neo-noir that pays tribute to classic detective cinema while exploring the darker side of a glamorous city.

title: Gudiya Ki Cycle
synopsis: Ten-year-old Gudiya lives in a village in Bundelkhand and walks six kilometres each way to school. When the state announces free bicycles for girls who top their exams, she studies harder than anyone, comes first in her class and becomes the proud owner of a shining new cycle. A week later it is stolen from outside the village temple. Nobody seems to care very much, and the police laugh at her complaint. Determined to get it back, Gudiya teams up with her younger brother Chhotu and a retired postman who knows every road in the district. Their search takes them through weekly markets, scrap dealers' yards and a travelling circus. Along the way, Gudiya discovers that her father had been planning to sell the cycle to pay off a debt, and that the theft is more complicated than it looks. Simple, warm and gently funny, the film is a children's drama about education, dignity and the freedom that a bicycle can bring.

title: Saas Bahu Aur Startup
synopsis: Meera quits her job at a Gurugram tech company to start her own business, only to find that her most demanding investor is her mother-in-law, Kamla, a retired school principal who has put her entire savings into the venture. The start-up, an app connecting busy families with home-cooked meals made by local women, quickly runs into trouble: delivery riders get lost, cooks fight over recipes and a rival company with deep pockets copies every idea. Kamla turns up at every meeting with spreadsheets, opinions and an uncanny ability to charm investors, while Meera's husband, a nervous banker, tries to stay out of it. The two women clash over everything, from marketing plans to the colour of the logo, but slowly realise that together they make a formidable team. When a corporate buyout threatens to push the cooks out, they must decide what kind of company they really want to build. The film is a bright family comedy about ambition, generations and unlikely partnerships.

title: Siachen Ke Saat Din
synopsis: In the winter of 2005, a small team of Indian Army soldiers is stationed at a forward post on the Siachen Glacier, more than twenty thousand feet above sea level, where the cold and the altitude claim more lives than any enemy. Major Arjun Thakur, on his last posting before a staff job, leads a mixed group of seasoned mountain troops and nervous young recruits. When an avalanche buries part of the post and cuts off communication, the survivors must hold their position and keep one another alive for seven days until rescue helicopters can fly. Rations run low, frostbite spreads and one soldier begins to lose his grip in the endless white. Back home, the Major's wife waits for news that does not come. Told without villains or speeches, the film is a stark survival drama about endurance, brotherhood and the ordinary people who guard the world's highest battlefield, with breathtaking mountain photography.

title: Araku Lo Aaru Rojulu
synopsis: Two strangers end up sharing a hired car from Visakhapatnam to the Araku Valley after both their bookings are cancelled. Bhargav is an uptight chartered accountant who has been ordered by his doctor to take a week off before he burns out. Sindhu is a talkative travel blogger with a tight deadline, a broken camera and a mysterious reason for visiting a particular village in the hills. Their plans to go separate ways keep failing, and over six days they find themselves exploring coffee plantations, waterfalls, tribal markets and limestone caves together, arguing about everything from music to money. Their driver, a self-taught philosopher who never stops talking, supplies the commentary. As the journey goes on, Sindhu's real purpose becomes clear: she is searching for the father she has never met. Bhargav, who has always played it safe, decides to help her. Breezy, scenic and charming, the film is a romantic road comedy about slowing down and finding what you did not know you were looking for.

title: Ooru Pedda
synopsis: For forty years, Bhupathi Rao has been the unchallenged elder of a large village in the Krishna district, settling disputes, controlling contracts and deciding who stands in every election. When the village president's seat is reserved for a woman from a Dalit family, his men pick a candidate they believe they can control: Saraswathi, a quiet anganwadi worker. But once in office, Saraswathi starts asking questions about missing funds, illegal sand mining and the land her own family lost years ago. Her son Ravi, a city-educated engineer, returns home to protect her, and the village slowly divides between those who fear the elder and those who see a chance for change. As the old man's sons turn to violence and a crucial vote approaches, Ravi and Saraswathi must decide how far they are willing to go. Mixing political drama with large-scale action, the film is a stirring story about power, caste and democracy at the grassroots.

title: Bhoota Bungalow
synopsis: Three broke friends in Hyderabad answer an online advertisement offering a luxury bungalow on the outskirts of the city for almost no rent. The catch, which they learn too late, is that every previous tenant left within a week claiming the house was haunted. Determined not to lose their deposit, the friends decide to stay, prove the ghost is fake and perhaps make some money by livestreaming the whole thing. Their plan goes badly wrong when the ghost turns out to be real, very opinionated and the spirit of a 1970s film actress who died in the house before her last film was released. She refuses to leave until that final movie is screened, and she expects the friends to make it happen. The trio find themselves hunting for a lost film print, dealing with a greedy property dealer and a fake exorcist, and growing fond of their glamorous, demanding housemate. The film is a lively horror comedy with songs, slapstick and a surprisingly touching ending.

title: Tirupati Tigers XI
synopsis: The Tirupati Tigers are the worst side in an amateur cricket league in Andhra Pradesh, a group of middle-aged clerks, shopkeepers and one retired umpire who have not won a match in six seasons. When their captain, a bank clerk named Prasad, learns that the ground they play on will be sold to a mall developer unless the team wins the league, he recruits his daughter Divya, a talented cricketer recently dropped from the state squad, as coach. Divya has no patience for the team's excuses, and she is nursing a disappointment of her own. Training sessions turn into comedy, with fielders who cannot run, bowlers who cannot aim and a wicketkeeper who is afraid of the ball. Slowly, under Divya's tough coaching, the team begins to improve, and the strained father-daughter relationship heals along the way. The film is a feel-good sports comedy with a big final match and plenty of affection for ordinary people who refuse to give up on something they love.

title: Mysuru Masala Murders
synopsis: During the ten days of Dasara in Mysuru, the city is lit up, the palace glows every night and the hotels are packed with tourists. At a family-run heritage guesthouse, a pompous celebrity chef judging a food contest collapses at the dinner table, poisoned. Retired schoolteacher Gundu Rao, who has read every detective novel in the city library, happens to be staying there with his granddaughter Pallavi, an impatient journalism student. When the local inspector arrests the guesthouse's cook, an old friend of Gundu Rao, he decides to investigate himself. The suspects include rival contestants, a food blogger with a grudge, a businessman who wanted to buy the guesthouse and the chef's long-suffering assistant. Between procession days, palace illuminations and plates of steaming dosas, grandfather and granddaughter piece together clues hidden in recipes. Cosy, colourful and full of local flavour, the film is a light comedy whodunit that celebrates its city as much as its mystery.

title: Banni Marada Kelage
synopsis: Under the old banni tree at the centre of a small village in north Karnataka, the village elders have met for generations to settle disputes. When the council's ageing head, Shivappa, falls ill, his granddaughter Gowri, a law graduate who has just failed her judicial service exam, reluctantly takes his place for the summer. At first the villagers ignore her, preferring the advice of a self-important landlord. But Gowri begins resolving cases in unexpected ways, from a quarrel over a wandering buffalo to a land dispute between two brothers and a marriage proposal that nobody else dares to question. Her rulings start to change the village, and not everyone is happy about it. Meanwhile, Gowri's own family pressures her to marry and give up her ambitions. Gentle, episodic and full of earthy humour, the film is a warm village drama about justice, common sense and a young woman discovering that the law is about people as much as books.

title: Bengaluru 2047
synopsis: In 2047, Bengaluru has run out of water. The lakes are gone, the borewells are dry, and water arrives in armed tankers run by a private corporation that rations it according to each citizen's credit score. Sathya is a tanker driver who knows every route through the parched city and keeps his head down to protect his young daughter. When he discovers that his company is hoarding water in a hidden reservoir beneath an abandoned tech park while people in the slums die of thirst, he is pulled into a resistance movement led by Meghana, a former hydrologist who once warned the city government about this exact crisis. Their plan to expose the corporation sends them through drained tunnels, guarded compounds and the cracked beds of the city's famous lakes. Grim but never hopeless, the film is a science-fiction thriller that imagines a near-future water crisis with chilling plausibility, asking who really owns a city's most basic resource.

title: Hockey Hudugiyaru
synopsis: In the coffee-growing district of Kodagu, hockey is almost a religion, and every village has its own team. Seventeen-year-old Dechu is the best striker in her school, but her family wants her to stop playing and concentrate on exams. When the school's girls' team is barred from the district championship because it cannot afford proper equipment, the players take matters into their own hands. They raise money by picking coffee, selling homemade pickles and organising a charity match against the boys' team. Their coach, a former national player who walked away from the sport after an injury, is reluctant to get involved again. As the championship approaches, the team faces injuries, rivalries, family resistance and a heavily funded side from Bengaluru. Packed with energetic match sequences and misty hillside scenery, the film is a spirited sports drama that celebrates the hockey culture of Kodagu and a group of girls who refuse to be benched.

title: Honey and Static
synopsis: On a windswept stretch of New Zealand's South Island, Bridget Grant keeps three hundred beehives on her late father's farm and speaks to almost nobody. Her only company is the local community radio station, where an overnight host named Tomás plays obscure records and reads out listeners' messages. When a disease threatens her hives and she needs help moving them, the person who answers her notice turns out to be Tomás himself, a former journalist from Buenos Aires who took the job to escape a scandal. The two spend a summer moving hives across valleys, arguing about music and slowly letting down their guard. But when an investor offers to buy the farm and a reporter from Tomás's past tracks him down, both must decide whether to keep hiding. Gentle, wry and filled with wide landscapes and humming bees, the film is a quiet romance about grief, second chances and the courage to be heard again.

title: Blind Corner in Lisbon
synopsis: Former intelligence officer Nathan Cole has spent five years running a quiet bookshop in Lisbon, convinced that his old employers have forgotten him. Then a woman he once trained, Anjali Rao, walks into the shop with a bullet wound and a memory card holding the names of agents working undercover across Europe. Within an hour, both of them are being hunted by mercenaries, local police and Nathan's former boss, who insists that Anjali is a traitor. Nathan has to decide whether to believe the woman bleeding in his back room or the agency he once trusted with his life. The chase sends them through the steep tiled streets and tram lines of Lisbon, onto a cargo ship and into a fado bar where every face may belong to an enemy. Tightly plotted and grounded in practical stunts, the film is a classic spy thriller about loyalty, betrayal and a man who cannot outrun the life he thought he had left behind.

title: Starlight Diner on Route 9
synopsis: Gloria Benitez has run the Starlight Diner on a lonely highway in New Mexico for twenty-six years, serving pie and coffee to truckers, tourists and the occasional lost musician. When a new interstate bypass threatens to make her road irrelevant, she decides to throw one last anniversary party before closing for good. Over a single day and night, a parade of regulars and strangers passes through the diner: a long-haul driver who has secretly loved her for years, a runaway teenager, a struggling country singer, a stranded family and her estranged son, who arrives with news she does not want to hear. Each brings a story, and by midnight the party has turned into something much bigger than anyone planned. Funny, bittersweet and full of small-town warmth, the film is an ensemble dramedy about endings, beginnings and the places that hold communities together, set to a soundtrack of old jukebox favourites and original songs.

title: The Hollow Choir
synopsis: In a small mining village in the Welsh valleys, the local male voice choir has sung at every funeral, wedding and festival for over a century. When the choir's ageing director dies suddenly, his niece Ffion, a disillusioned London music teacher, returns home to lead the singers through their centenary concert. During rehearsals in the old chapel, she hears an extra voice joining them, a deep, mournful tenor that nobody else admits to hearing. Soon choir members begin disappearing one by one, and the hymns they sing take on a sinister meaning. Ffion uncovers a forgotten mining disaster and a pact made by the village's founders that binds the choir's music to the men who died underground. As the concert draws near, she must work out what the voice wants before the whole choir is lost. Atmospheric and unsettling, the film is a folk horror story that uses music, grief and buried secrets to build its slow, creeping dread.

title: Uchakkanji Teacher
synopsis: For twenty-five years, Kousalya has cooked the free midday meal at a government school in a village near Pathanamthitta, serving rice gruel and green gram to children who often have nothing else to eat all day. Everyone calls her Uchakkanji Teacher, though she never finished school herself. When a new headmaster decides to outsource the meals to a central kitchen run by a contractor, Kousalya is told her services are no longer needed. Within weeks the children are complaining about cold, tasteless food, attendance drops and one boy faints in class. Kousalya's quiet protest, cooking at her own home and carrying meals to the school gate, grows into a campaign that draws in parents, a curious journalist and eventually the education department. Her grandson, who has always been embarrassed by her humble job, slowly comes to see her differently. Simple and moving, the film is a heartfelt drama about food, dignity and the unsung people who keep public institutions running.

title: Kudamattam Kollai
synopsis: Every year at Thrissur's grand temple festival, hundreds of thousands of people gather to watch caparisoned elephants and the dazzling exchange of colourful parasols. This year, a gang of small-time crooks has a plan: under cover of the noise and crowds, they will rob a jeweller's vault on the edge of the festival grounds. The gang is led by Sunny, a smooth talker who has never pulled off anything bigger than a chit-fund scam, and includes a nervous mahout, a retired bank guard and a pickpocket who cannot stop stealing from his own partners. Unfortunately, a rival gang has the same idea, a tough police officer has been tipped off, and the jeweller's daughter is far smarter than any of them. As fireworks, drums and elephants fill the night, the heist collapses into a chain of double-crosses and comic disasters. Fast, noisy and colourful, the film is a crowd-pleasing heist comedy that uses one of Kerala's biggest festivals as its playground.

title: Varanmaar Wanted
synopsis: Bindu runs a struggling matrimonial agency from a tiny office above a bakery in Kottayam, matching couples with an old register, a great deal of intuition and her mother's horoscope charts. When a slick online marriage app opens in town, her clients disappear, and she has three months to save the business. In desperation, she takes on an impossible case: finding a husband for Ammu, a fiercely independent veterinary doctor whose wealthy family has rejected every proposal so far. Helping her is Jerry, an awkward graphic designer who builds the agency a website and harbours a crush on Bindu that he cannot bring himself to admit. As the search brings a parade of hopeless grooms, family feuds and disastrous first meetings, Bindu begins to wonder whether arranged marriage is really about matching horoscopes or understanding people. The film is a breezy romantic comedy full of eccentric characters and gentle satire about weddings, families and the business of finding love.

title: Moonnam Naal Kadalil
synopsis: Five fishermen from Vizhinjam set out in a small boat for what should be a two-day trip. On the second night, a cyclone that the forecasts failed to predict tears across the Arabian Sea, wrecking their engine and leaving them adrift with little food or water. The crew is led by Pathrose, an ageing fisherman in his final season, along with his headstrong nephew Joby, a migrant worker from Odisha and two brothers who have not spoken to each other in years. As days pass on the open sea, they battle storms, hunger, sharks and their own fear, while their families on shore wait in a church hall for news and argue with officials about the search. Drawing on the experiences of coastal communities battered by storms, the film is a tense survival drama about solidarity, faith and the bonds formed when everything else has been lost, with remarkable sequences filmed on open water.

title: Ilaveyil Kaalam
synopsis: Palakkad, 1996. Ten classmates at a government school spend their final year together before board exams scatter them. The story follows Hari, a shy boy who writes poems he never shows anyone, his loud best friend Rafeeq, and Anitha, the new girl from Bombay whose arrival changes their small group. Through cricket matches in paddy fields, cinema trips, cassette swapping, a school drama competition and a sudden accident, they learn about friendship, first love and loss. Twenty-five years later, a messaging group brings them back together for a reunion at their old school, and the adult Hari must finally face what happened that year. Told in two timelines with warm, sun-soaked visuals and a nostalgic soundtrack, the film is a gentle coming-of-age drama about growing up in the years before mobile phones, and about friendships that shape a person long after school ends.

title: Theru Koothu Raja
synopsis: Rajamani has performed in therukoothu, the traditional street theatre of Tamil Nadu, for forty years, playing kings, demons and gods in all-night performances in village squares. Now in his sixties, he watches audiences dwindle as young people turn to phones and cinema. When a well-known film director scouting locations spots him in a performance, Rajamani is offered a small role in a big-budget film. In the city, he struggles with retakes, vanity vans and a young star who treats him as a prop. Back in the village, his son resents the time he spends away, and his troupe begins to fall apart without him. As the shoot nears its climax, Rajamani must decide where he truly belongs. Combining vibrant performance sequences with gentle comedy about the film industry, the film is a warm, affectionate drama about folk art, ageing and the dignity of a performer who has given his whole life to the stage.

title: Ennore Kadal
synopsis: Muthu is a fisherman in Ennore, on the northern edge of Chennai, where the sea is ringed by power plants, ports and factories. One night an oil tanker collision spills thick black crude along the coast. Officials say the situation is under control, but Muthu's nets come up coated in oil, fish die in their thousands and children in the village fall sick. Determined to find out what really happened, he teams up with Karthiga, an environmental lawyer, and a young engineer at the port who has secretly kept the real data. Together they uncover a cover-up involving a shipping company, a corrupt port official and a cleanup contractor making money from the disaster. As they gather evidence, the fishing families face intimidation, bribes and threats. Shot along a scarred shoreline, the film is a gripping environmental thriller about the cost of development and the communities left to pay for it.

title: Muhurtham Missing
synopsis: The wedding of Arjun and Sandhya has been planned to the last detail by their families, down to an auspicious muhurtham at 6.12 in the morning that the astrologer insists must not be missed by a single minute. On the morning of the wedding, the groom vanishes from his room. While the bride's family suspects cold feet and the groom's mother suspects a curse, Arjun's two best friends and Sandhya's sharp-tongued younger sister race across Chennai to find him before the appointed time. Their search, involving a missing car, a tipsy uncle, a lost silk saree and a temple elephant, reveals that Arjun's disappearance is far stranger than anyone imagined. Meanwhile Sandhya calmly prepares for the ceremony, convinced there is more going on than she has been told. A fast-paced ensemble comedy set over one frantic morning, the film is full of mix-ups, family chaos and affectionate jokes about weddings and astrology.

title: Negative Reel 1979
synopsis: When an old film-processing laboratory in Chennai is being cleared for demolition, archivist Nila finds a can of undeveloped negatives labelled with the name of a horror film that was never released. Curious, she develops the footage with her colleague Selvam and discovers scenes that match no script: shadowy figures in the background, a woman screaming at the camera and glimpses of the laboratory itself. The film's crew, she learns, disappeared during production in 1979. As the pair digitise more reels, strange things begin happening in their own lives: faces appear in mirrors, phone recordings fill with whispers and the lab's long-dead projectionist seems to be watching them. Nila's investigation leads to the film's ageing producer, who has kept a terrible secret for decades. Building dread through grainy celluloid, flickering projector light and inventive sound design, the film is a horror story about cinema, memory and images that refuse to stay buried.

title: Banaras Ki Billi
synopsis: In the narrow lanes of Banaras, a fat orange cat named Raja has been the unofficial mascot of a famous sweet shop for years. When the shop's owner dies, he leaves his entire fortune to the cat, with instructions that whoever takes the best care of Raja for a year will inherit the shop. Suddenly the animal has a great many admirers: the owner's greedy nephews, a struggling boatman named Bittu who used to feed it leftovers, an ambitious lawyer and a television anchor hungry for a story. When Raja vanishes during the festival of lamps on the ghats, a frantic chase begins through temples, wrestling pits and rooftop kite battles. Bittu, helped by the shop's clever cashier Rani, must find the cat before the nephews do, while learning that the old man's will was really a test of character. Bright, playful and full of local colour, the film is a family adventure comedy with plenty of heart and a thoroughly unbothered feline star.

title: Arzi No. 4417
synopsis: Rajkumar Singh is a mid-level clerk in a district office in Uttar Pradesh who has never broken a rule or asked an awkward question. When his teenage daughter dies in a bus accident on a road that was officially repaired three times, he files a simple right-to-information application asking where the money went. The reply is evasive. He files another, and then another. Each answer leads him deeper into a network of fake contractors, ghost projects and powerful local politicians. His colleagues avoid him, his wife fears for the family, and anonymous callers warn him to stop. With the help of Shruti, a young local journalist, and a retired engineer who knows exactly how the system works, Rajkumar becomes an unlikely activist. Celebrating ordinary citizens who use information as a weapon, the film is a tense, grounded drama about grief, accountability and the quiet power of asking questions that nobody wants answered.

title: Metro Ki Aakhri Seat
synopsis: Every morning at 8.14, Aditya catches the Delhi Metro from Dwarka to his insurance job in Connaught Place, and every morning the same young woman takes the last empty seat in the coach just before he can see her face. Over months of commuting, he learns about her only in glimpses: the books she reads, the songs leaking from her earphones, the doodles she leaves on the misted window. When she accidentally leaves her sketchbook on the train, Aditya sets out to return it and, with help from a talkative metro guard and his own meddling grandmother, begins tracking down the mystery artist. Meanwhile the artist, Naina, has her own reasons for leaving clues behind. Told largely through the rhythms of the city's metro, with its crowds, announcements and stations, the film is a charming modern romance about connection in a crowded city and the courage it takes to simply say hello.

title: Kachchh Ki Kaali Raat
synopsis: In the vast salt desert of the Rann of Kutch, border security officer Rudra Pratap Singh is tracking a smuggling network that moves weapons and drugs across the marshes at night. When a young informer is killed and a tourist couple go missing during the region's famous winter festival, Rudra is sent to investigate alongside Fatima, a determined local police inspector who knows every village and community in the area. Their search uncovers a ruthless trafficker known only as the Seth, who has bought loyalty from officials, camel traders and fishermen alike. As a full moon approaches, the night the smugglers plan their biggest consignment, Rudra and Fatima must work out whom they can trust before the salt flats turn into a battlefield. With striking white landscapes, tense night-time chases and a pulsing score, the film is a gritty action thriller about duty, corruption and the people who live on the edge of a border.

title: Share Auto Sundaram
synopsis: Sundaram has driven a share auto between Vijayawada's bus stand and its railway station for nineteen years, squeezing in seven passengers at a time and dispensing life advice whether anyone wants it or not. When a ride-hailing company launches electric autos in the city, his income collapses just as his daughter's college fees fall due. Desperate, Sundaram joins the app, only to watch his ratings drop every time he starts one of his famous lectures. Meanwhile, his regular passengers, a nurse, a vegetable seller, a college boy and a retired professor, miss their noisy daily rides and decide to help him in their own chaotic ways. Their scheme to win a city-wide contest for the best driver sets off a chain of comic misadventures, rivalries and unexpected friendships. Warm and lively, the film is a working-class comedy about technology, community and a stubborn man learning to adapt without losing his voice.

title: Kakatiya Khadgam
synopsis: In the thirteenth century, the Kakatiya kingdom of Warangal is famed for its temples, lakes and the skill of its warriors.
